data.narrative:
Nth Cycle operates in Climate & Energy at the Growth + Offtake stage, having raised $60M in equity alongside a $1.1B 10-year offtake agreement with Trafigura. The valuation universe comprises 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA) and 8 private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable here. The Climate & Energy sector contains only 9 same-sector peers overall, but none satisfy the necessary screening criteria of matching stage, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial distortion given the heterogeneity in business models, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines across climate tech. The single public comparable provides limited directional guidance without a broader public reference set.

The offtake agreement with Trafigura—a $1.1B commitment over ten years—constitutes a material revenue anchor that should inform valuation, though converting this to an enterprise value requires assumptions on margins, discount rates, and probability of contract fulfillment that lie outside the quantitative data provided. A credible valuation range cannot be derived from the available data without applying subjective modeling assumptions. Further analysis would require either (1) detailed financials and unit economics from Nth Cycle, (2) expanded peer financials allowing stage-matched comparisons, or (3) DCF modeling of the offtake agreement's present value contribution.
